criteria.commensurate: The cost falls only where a settlement's share allows a passage, and grows with the budget. 40hh s25 (budget 9) pays +1.1 s CPU homesteads, +21.6% wall, for 5 tight-seated households: 1 reached across a yard and 4 re-laid at their tight seat with a way of their own (relay keeps them seated, so the work buys seats in the finished map). 40hh s47's +1.1 s is the existing web drawing the passage's layout, not new code (anchors stubbed: web 2.50 vs 2.46). The same layout effect moves 40hh s4 the other way (-9.4%). The bookend is -0.9% over all legs and +5.2% at 40hh. For the feature's whole deliverable, that is proportionate.
criteria.necessary: The cost is the feature's own function. FR-002/FR-003 ask for households reached across a neighbor's yard within the rolled share, which the GM's request (go with what the research bears out, Wigmore 1892) opened. The MODE 1 ruling made the growth offer tight seats (R6, R7). The plan review required asking every layout of the holding (landlocked) and the recheck on the finished seating (recheck_passages). Removing the passage alone (passage_share 0) puts every crossing back on main in the reviewer's 3 alternated takes: 40hh s25 homesteads 1.87-1.96 vs main 1.81-1.84; 40hh s47 web 1.23-1.30 vs 1.31-1.34; 20hh s25 and s47 homesteads 0.75-0.83 vs 0.68-0.82.
criteria.no_way_around: No cheaper form that keeps the passages is known from the data. Each measured lever cuts passages or saves nothing: offering tight seats only behind a no-corridor seat (3 vs 16 passages), capping tries (passages came from the 3rd to the 42nd try), the yard-side bearing only (12 of 16 passages, still +18%), TIGHT_TREE_FT 80/120/160 (no change at s25), and remembering landlocked's proof (0.05 s, reverted). The reviewer's profile at 40hh s25 puts about half the growth in route searches (search 2.12 vs 0.66 s cumulative, 472 vs 113 calls), mostly failing searches that flood the 320 px reach to prove a seat has no way of its own. The rest is the 160 extra placements' layouts and settles (try_place 4.83 vs 2.84 s). One untried direction remains: a cheaper negative proof, such as one reachability raster per standing state shared across searches. It is a redesign of the search, not a lever: the grid is laid from each door because a map-aligned grid lost the narrow ways (feature 314 R4, 16.4 s vs 5.9). Its saving is bounded by the searches' share, about 0.5 s of the 1.1 s at s25. A follow-up could price it, but no cheaper form is demonstrated now.
